Ok, I promised @middle_path that I would put together a post on how I'm doing shit loads of seed tapes quickly.

Start off with a roll of generic paper towels. Nothing fancy, so super absorbency or anything with extra chemicals or perfumes. Just generic shitty paper towels. If they are full size sheets, pull off a segment of four. If they are the half sheets, pull off eight. The number is subjective, but I've found this length to be the easiest to work with.

Turn them into an accordion like this.
https://imgoat.com/uploads/336dcbab05/194126.jpg

Cut them up into strips like this.
https://imgoat.com/uploads/336dcbab05/194124.jpg

Run a layer of glue stick down HALF of the paper towel strip. For full size sheets it would be two of the segments, for the half sheets it would be four. Now, you can do glue on the full length of the strip, but you are going to burn through glue like crazy and there is really no need for it.

Plop your seeds onto the glue in whatever fashion you wish.
https://imgoat.com/uploads/336dcbab05/194125.jpg

Fold over the other half of the strip and press it down firmly. You are not worried about gluing the seeds to the strip, so much as making an envelope of paper towel around the seed. These segments of strips can be glued together into one long strip, or can be pulled apart to mix in other types of seeds.
https://imgoat.com/uploads/336dcbab05/194129.jpg

Now, if you want to make a seed strip for a mixed border, here is what I do. I make an absolute shit load of segments for each seed type. In this case, marigold, zinnia, and poppy. These will form a border around my entire garden, as well as a few internal subdivisions to segregate plants that seem to attract pests (fuck you mustard and your ability to attract harlequin bugs). Glue these segments together into whatever manner you want.
https://imgoat.com/uploads/336dcbab05/194127.jpg

Once you get going with it, it's pretty easy to turn it into an assembly line process and crank out ass loads of seed strips.
https://imgoat.com/uploads/336dcbab05/194128.jpg
